[8, 9] The price adjustment for the Model 3 was specifically linked to news that it would only qualify for half of the $7,500 tax credit due to these new rules. [9] Analysts also suggested the cuts were a measure to maintain market share and stimulate demand amid increasing competition and signs of slowing sales growth. This series of updates unified the vision and planning stack for both city and highway driving, replacing the legacy highway stack that was over four years old. [5] The goal of this major re-architecture was to enable more intelligent vehicle behaviors, smoother control, and improved decision-making in various scenarios, such as better handling of high-curvature roads and close cut-in cases. [5] FSD Beta v11.3.6 (2022.45.15) began rolling out around April 8, 2023, primarily containing bug fixes and subtle improvements without new release notes. [2] Reviews from testers on v11.3.6 were mixed; while some noted perceptible improvements in smoothness and the timing of lane changes, persistent issues such as phantom braking and incorrect lane selection were also reported. Prediction target period: from 2023-12-24 to 2024-03-10. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> To reduce wait times at busy Supercharger locations in the United States, Tesla implemented a 'congestion fee' of $1.00 per minute. This fee applies when a station is experiencing high usage and a vehicle's battery is charged to 90% or more. Initially, there were indications the fee might apply at an 80% charge level, but the official rollout set the threshold at 90%. The policy is designed to discourage charging to 100%, a process that significantly slows down as the battery nears full capacity, thereby increasing charger availability for more drivers. Drivers receive an alert through the Tesla app when the conditions for the fee are met and are given a five-minute grace period to move their vehicle before charges begin to accrue. This fee replaces the standard 'idle fee' at designated high-traffic stations and also applies to owners with free Supercharging privileges. <2> Tesla released its third-quarter financial results after the market closed on October 18, 2023. Concurrent with the financial data, the company announced its production and delivery figures for the third quarter of 2023, reporting the production of 430,488 vehicles and the delivery of 435,059. Tesla attributed a sequential decrease in volume to planned factory shutdowns for upgrades, including the rollout of the updated Model 3 at Gigafactory Shanghai. [1, 2] <3> Tesla released software update 2023.32.4, aimed at enhancing the standard Autopilot experience by integrating improved visualizations previously available only in the Full Self-Driving (FSD) Beta program. A key feature of this update is the introduction of dynamic vehicle sizing on the display, which allows the system to more accurately represent the varying widths, heights, and lengths of surrounding vehicles through its 3D models. <4> Tesla announced its financial results for the second quarter of 2023 on July 19, 2023, reporting record vehicle production of 479,700 and deliveries of 466,140. [2, 6] The company's total revenue for the quarter, which ended June 30, 2023, rose 47% year-over-year to $24.93 billion. [2] Net income was $2.7 billion, a 20% increase from the same period in the previous year. The company achieved an operating margin of 9.6%. [2] <5> Tesla announced the production of the first Cybertruck at its Gigafactory in Texas on July 15, 2023, a milestone confirmed by a company social media post showing the vehicle surrounded by workers. This event marked the beginning of pilot production for the electric pickup truck, which was initially unveiled as a prototype in November 2019. Following this initial build, serial production and the first customer deliveries commenced on November 30, 2023. Despite the production start, analysts expressed caution regarding the production ramp-up, with some predicting that meaningful volumes would not be achieved until 2025 or later. In May 2023, CEO Elon Musk had stated an ambitious annual production target of 250,000 to 500,000 vehicles once mass production was underway. <6> General Motors announced a collaboration with Tesla on June 8, 2023, to integrate the North American Charging Standard (NACS) into its electric vehicles and provide access to Tesla's Supercharger network. [8, 10] The agreement allows GM EV drivers access to the Tesla Supercharger network across North America. This access, initially planned for early 2024, GM still plans to build new electric vehicles with the NACS charge port integrated directly, eliminating the need for an adapter, starting in 2025. [8, 9, 14] <7> A cascade of major automakers announced decisions to adopt Tesla's North American Charging Standard (NACS), marking a pivotal shift towards a unified electric vehicle charging system in the U.S. and Canada. The trend began in earnest when General Motors announced its adoption on June 8, 2023. Following this, Honda formalized its agreement on September 7, 2023. BMW Group, including Mini and Rolls-Royce, followed suit with an announcement on October 17, 2023, and Toyota and Lexus made their decision public on October 19, 2023. These agreements grant EV drivers from the adopting brands access to Tesla's extensive Supercharger network, significantly expanding charging options. Most manufacturers plan to integrate NACS ports directly into their new vehicle models starting in 2025. For existing vehicles equipped with the Combined Charging System (CCS), automakers will provide adapters to enable access to the Supercharger network, with availability beginning in 2024 for some and 2025 for others. <8> Tesla released its financial results for the first quarter of 2023 on April 19, 2023, after the market closed. The release included the Q1 2023 Update Letter, which detailed revenues of $23.33 billion and a non-GAAP EPS of $0.85, meeting analyst expectations. This announcement was followed by a live question and answer webcast with management at 4:30 p.m. Central Time to discuss the results and outlook. The company highlighted a 24% year-over-year growth in revenue for the quarter but also a decrease in operating income to $2.7 billion. During the webcast, executives discussed the company's focus on growing production volume, investments in vehicle software, and progress on its next-generation platform. <9> In early April 2023, Tesla enacted its sixth price reduction of the year, affecting several of its popular electric vehicle models. The cost of the Model 3 Rear-Wheel Drive and Performance versions were each lowered by $1,000. [9] Additionally, the Model Y Long Range and Performance models saw a price drop of $2,000 each. This strategic move was widely seen as a response to anticipated changes in U.S. federal EV tax credits, which were set to be impacted by new, stricter battery component and mineral sourcing regulations. [8, 9] The price adjustment for the Model 3 was specifically linked to news that it would only qualify for half of the $7,500 tax credit due to these new rules. [9] Analysts also suggested the cuts were a measure to maintain market share and stimulate demand amid increasing competition and signs of slowing sales growth. [2, 8]

Tesla, Inc., was filed against Tesla in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California on June 27, 2024. The suit, brought by former employee Sharon Lane Chin, alleges that Tesla violated the federal and California Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Acts. The complaint claims the company failed to provide the legally mandated 60 days' advance written notice for mass layoffs that began around April 14, 2024, which affected approximately 14,000 employees. The lawsuit seeks to represent thousands of laid-off workers and aims to recover 60 days of back pay and benefits. <2> Tesla has initiated two separate recalls for its 2024 Cybertruck, which collectively mark the third and fourth recalls for the electric pickup. The first recall affects 11,688 vehicles due to a front windshield wiper motor that can fail because of excessive electrical current, potentially reducing visibility and increasing crash risk. The second recall involves 11,383 Cybertrucks for a trunk bed trim piece, called the sail applique, that may have been improperly attached and could detach, creating a road hazard. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) published the recall reports on June 25, 2024. Tesla became aware of the wiper issue in February 2024 and the trim issue in December 2023. The company will replace the wiper motor and replace or rework the trim piece at no cost to owners, with notification letters scheduled to be sent in August. <3> Several Tesla shareholders, including the Cleveland Bakers and Teamsters Pension Fund, filed a lawsuit in Delaware's Chancery Court against CEO Elon Musk and the company's board of directors, alleging a breach of fiduciary duty. The complaint, filed on June 13, 2024, claims Musk has been improperly diverting scarce resources and talent from Tesla to his competing artificial intelligence company, xAI, which he founded in 2023. Specific allegations include poaching key AI-focused employees, such as Tesla's computer vision team lead, and directing shipments of critical Nvidia GPU chips originally intended for Tesla to xAI and his social media company, X. The lawsuit cites Musk's own public statements about preferring to build AI and robotics products outside of Tesla unless granted approximately 25% voting control of the company. Shareholders argue the board has failed in its duty by allowing Musk's "brazen disloyalty" and enabling him to build billions in AI-related value at a separate company.
